newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Ommeren sees growth in chemicals and gas.
newsitem.headline: Ommeren sees growth in chemicals and gas.

text.p: Dutch shipping and tank storage firm Koninklijke van Ommeren NV said on Thursday future growth would come in chemicals and gas activities.

"Our results in chemicals were a bit lower than the exceptional 1995 year, .... (but) margins should be better and that is why we can set the target of 15 percent for return on equity," Chairman Carel van den Driest told a results news conference.
He added that Van Ommeren expected to make investment of around 200 million guilders this year, much of it in chemical storage facilities in Asia.
The company would maintain its focus on storage, but also hoped to grow in its shipping activities. There too, chemicals would provide the key to growth.
"In shipping too we are concentrating on chemicals," he said.
Participating interests in Iver Ships and United Tankers had enhanced Van Ommeren's chemicals' involvement.
The company's expansion of chemicals interests is partly a reflection of depressed margins on mineral oil storage, but it said it had no plans to scale down activity in that sector.
"The further expansion of our chemical activities has not been at the expense of our strong position in the storage and transport of mineral oils," Van den Driest said.
Van Ommeren's gas storage and transport, though smaller than its chemicals activities, would provide the company with similar prospects for growth,
"We also have a great expectation in gas. The market in Europe can grow enormously," Van den Driest said.

Van Ommeren is also seeking to increase its role in expanding markets, said executive board member Rick van Westenbrugge. He said Asia -- notably China and India -- and South America, especially Brazil, should prove the company with healthy returns.
"In gas there is enormous growth and we will transfer our knowledge from Europe to these areas," he said.
Earlier, Van Ommeren posted 1996 net profit of 94.4 million guilders, up from 1995's 80.3 million. The dividend was raised to 2.50 guilders per share from 2.00 in 1995.
